function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick snapshot of the **next big festivals happening in the United States** (as of mid‑2026).  I’ve pulled together the most widely‑publicized events that are scheduled to take place in the coming weeks, along with a short description, dates, venue, and where you can find more details.

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | What to Expect | Where to Get Tickets / Info |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | **April 20–22, 2026** | Indio, California (Empire Polo Club) | 2‑day music & art festival featuring top‑tier rock, hip‑hop, indie, and electronic acts, plus large‑scale art installations. | [coachella.com](https://www.coachella.com) |

| 4 | **Burning Man** | **Aug 28–Sep 5, 2026** | Black Rock Desert, Nevada | 9‑day arts‑and‑community event featuring large-scale art installations, music, and a temporary city built from scratch. | [burningman.org](https://www.burningman.org) |
| 5 | **New York Film Festival** | **Sept 1–12, 2026** | New York City (Lincoln Center) | 12‑day showcase of world cinema, retrospectives, and special events. | [nyff.org](https://www.nyff.org) |
| 6 | **Taste of Chicago** | **Oct 14–16, 2026** | Chicago, Illinois | 3‑day food festival featuring chefs, cooking demos, and live music. | [tasteofchicago.com](https://www.tasteofchicago.com) |

### How to Find the “Next” Festival for Your Area

1. **Local Event Calendars** – Check city or county tourism sites (e.g., *Visit Los Angeles*, *San Diego Tourism Authority*).  
2. **Ticketing Platforms** – Sites like Ticketmaster, Eventbrite, and Live Nation list upcoming festivals by date and location.  
3. **Social Media & Newsletters** – Follow local venues, promoters, and community groups on Instagram/Twitter for real‑time updates.  
4. **Google “Upcoming festivals in [your city]”** – Often pulls a curated list from local news outlets.

---

#### Quick Tips for Attending

| Tip | Why It Helps |
|-----|--------------|
| **Buy tickets early** | Popular festivals sell out months in advance. |
| **Check travel & lodging** | Major festivals attract crowds; book hotels or campgrounds early. |
| **Plan your schedule** | Many festivals have multiple stages; map out must‑see acts. |
| **Pack essentials** | Sunscreen, water bottle, comfortable shoes, and a light jacket (weather can change). |
| **Stay hydrated & safe** | Follow festival health guidelines and keep an eye on your belongings. |

If you’re looking for a specific type of festival (e.g., food, tech, indie music, cultural heritage), let me know and I can narrow the list further!
